content:
Mensuration is the most diagram-friendly chapter of Class 6 — perimeter and area of rectangles, squares, triangles and composite L-shapes, plus fencing and tiling costs. Here is what the IMO Class 6 mensuration chapter tests, the formulas, and a free 10-question test with figures.

What the Class 6 Maths Olympiad Mensuration chapter tests

  • Perimeter of rectangles, squares, triangles and regular polygons
  • Area of rectangles and squares; counting grid squares
  • Composite (L-shaped) figures and paths
  • Fencing/tiling cost problems and unit choices

Key facts your child should know

  • P(rect) = 2(l + b); P(square) = 4 × side; regular polygon P = sides × length.
  • A(rect) = l × b; A(square) = side².
  • Split composite figures into rectangles and ADD the areas.
  • Fencing/border → perimeter; tiling/carpeting → area.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Using perimeter where the problem needs area (and vice-versa).
  • Forgetting inner cuts still count in an L-shape's perimeter.
  • Writing area in cm instead of sq cm.

faq.q: What is the perimeter of a rectangle 9 cm by 5 cm?
faq.a: 2 × (9 + 5) = 28 cm; its area is 9 × 5 = 45 sq cm.

faq.q: How do you find the area of an L-shaped figure?
faq.a: Split it into two rectangles, find each area, and add them.
